title: Seeing images and using AI safely · Level 3
slo: Distinguish major computer-vision tasks and explain the purpose of AI guardrails.

exercises.question_text: What area of AI analyzes photos, videos, and live camera feeds?

options.rationale: Computer vision is the broad AI area for analyzing visual input. That input includes photos, videos, and live camera feeds.
Information extraction finds specific details in content rather than broadly analyzing visual input. It does not name the overall AI area for images and video.
options.better_fit: Use it when extracting fields such as receipt totals or serial numbers.

feedback.intrinsic: This would focus on isolated details rather than visual analysis.
feedback.instructional: Computer vision is the broad area for analyzing visual input.

options.rationale: A multi-modal model is a particular model type that combines visual features with text. It is not the broad area that includes all visual analysis.
options.better_fit: Use it when image features and related text must produce a detailed description.

feedback.intrinsic: This would name a narrower model type.
feedback.instructional: Computer vision is the broader visual-analysis field.

options.rationale: Image classification is one task within computer vision. It predicts a main-subject label instead of naming the whole field.
options.better_fit: Use it when an image needs one main-subject label.

feedback.intrinsic: This would narrow the goal to labeling.
feedback.instructional: Image classification is a computer-vision task.

exercises.question_text: Which statements describe a multi-modal model? Select all that apply.

options.text: It combines visual features with text descriptions.
options.rationale: Combining visual features with associated text descriptions defines this model type. The combination supports richer outputs.

options.text: It can generate comprehensive image descriptions.
options.rationale: The model can use its combined information to produce comprehensive descriptions. This is more than a single label.

options.text: It only assigns a main-subject label.
options.rationale: Assigning one main-subject label is image classification. A multi-modal model can generate broader descriptions.
options.better_fit: Use it when a single image category is sufficient.

feedback.intrinsic: This would reduce a description to one label.
feedback.instructional: Multi-modal models combine visual and text information.

options.rationale: Identifying object locations is object detection. A multi-modal model is not limited to locations.
options.better_fit: Use it when specific object positions are required.

feedback.intrinsic: The comprehensive description would be missing.
feedback.instructional: Object detection finds locations; multi-modal models describe images.

exercises.explanation: Correct—multi-modal models combine visual features and associated text.

exercises.question_text: Semantic segmentation identifies the individual pixels that belong to an object.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing false would remove the key pixel-level distinction.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Semantic segmentation identifies individual object pixels.

exercises.explanation: Correct—pixel-level identification is its defining feature.

exercises.question_text: A safeguard that reduces the risk of harmful generated content is a ___.

parts.text: A safeguard that reduces the risk of harmful generated content is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected term would not identify the named safeguard.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use content filters for safeguards that reduce harmful generated content.

exercises.explanation: Content filters are a named safeguard for reducing harmful-content risk.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the pieces into a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The sentence does not clearly express the relationship.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the field, followed by what it analyzes.

exercises.correct_answer: Computer vision analyzes visual input from cameras and uploaded images
exercises.explanation: The sentence first names the field, then its action, then examples of input.

exercises.question_text: A chat-product owner can fund either a one-time output filter or a lifecycle program with filters, design reviews, implementation checks, and operational monitoring. The product may generate harmful or illegal replies. Which decisions best fit responsible AI? Select all that apply.

options.text: Use content filters to reduce harmful outputs.
options.rationale: Content filters directly help reduce harmful generated outputs. They are an appropriate safeguard for the stated risk.

options.text: Fund guardrails from conception through operation.
options.rationale: Responsible AI requires attention from conception through design, implementation, and operation. A lifecycle program addresses that requirement.

options.text: Rely on a one-time filter and skip later monitoring.
options.rationale: A one-time filter does not satisfy lifecycle-wide responsibility. Risks and system behavior must also be addressed during operation.
options.better_fit: A filter may be one component within an ongoing guardrail program.

feedback.intrinsic: New or overlooked risks could persist after release.
feedback.instructional: Responsible AI requires guardrails across the full lifecycle.

options.text: Only disclose that AI is used.
options.rationale: Disclosure supports transparency but does not itself reduce harmful or illegal outputs. It is insufficient for the owner's stated risk.
options.better_fit: Use disclosure when explaining that AI is used and communicating limitations.

feedback.intrinsic: Users may be informed while harmful outputs remain unmitigated.
feedback.instructional: Harmful-output risks need safeguards such as filters and lifecycle guardrails.

exercises.explanation: Correct—filters and lifecycle-wide guardrails best address the risk.

exercises.question_text: A system that produces comprehensive image descriptions from visual features and associated text is a ___.

parts.text: A system that produces comprehensive image descriptions from visual features and associated text is a

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The selected term would not name the model type that integrates both modalities.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Use multi-modal model when visual features and text descriptions are combined.

exercises.explanation: A multi-modal model combines visual features with associated text descriptions.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the pieces into a correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The relationship between the two tasks is unclear.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with semantic segmentation, then state that it extends object detection.

exercises.correct_answer: Semantic segmentation is an advanced form of object detection with pixel-level detail
exercises.explanation: The sentence explains segmentation's relationship to object detection and its higher level of detail.

exercises.question_text: Which computer-vision task identifies where specific objects appear in an image?

options.rationale: Object detection identifies specific objects and their locations in an image. Location is its defining output.
Image classification predicts a main-subject label. It does not show object positions.
options.better_fit: Use it when one main image label is needed.

feedback.intrinsic: The image would be labeled but object positions would be absent.

options.rationale: Semantic segmentation identifies individual object pixels. It is more detailed than merely locating an object.
options.better_fit: Use it when exact pixels belonging to an object are needed.

feedback.intrinsic: This would request pixel boundaries rather than locations.

options.rationale: A multi-modal model produces comprehensive descriptions using visual features and text. It is not defined by object positions.
options.better_fit: Use it for detailed written image descriptions.

feedback.intrinsic: The output could be descriptive without locating objects.
feedback.instructional: Choose object detection when location is essential.

exercises.question_text: Image classification learns from images labeled with their main subject.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Choosing false removes the labels needed to connect images to subjects.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Image classification trains on images labeled by main subject.

exercises.explanation: Correct—main-subject labels are used in training.

exercises.question_text: Which tasks can object detection perform? Select all that apply.

options.text: Find a product's location in a photo.
options.rationale: Object detection identifies where specific objects appear. A product location is a direct example.

options.text: Find specific objects in a camera feed.
options.rationale: Camera feeds are visual input in which object detection can find specified objects and their locations. This fits detection's purpose.
One main-subject label is the output of image classification. Detection focuses on specific objects and where they occur.
options.better_fit: Use it when an image needs one overall category.

feedback.intrinsic: This would lose the locations of individual objects.

options.text: Identify all pixels of an object.
options.rationale: Individual object pixels are identified by semantic segmentation. Detection does not require pixel-level boundaries.
options.better_fit: Use it when precise object boundaries are needed.

feedback.intrinsic: This adds pixel detail beyond a location need.

exercises.explanation: Correct—object detection finds objects and their locations.

exercises.question_text: What does image classification predict for an unlabeled image?

options.rationale: Image classification predicts the label that best represents an image's main subject. It does not identify locations or pixels.
Object detection identifies object locations. Classification instead returns a subject label.
options.better_fit: Use it when specific objects must be located.

feedback.intrinsic: The result would focus on positions, not a main label.

options.rationale: Semantic segmentation identifies individual pixels belonging to objects. Classification provides less detailed labeling.
options.better_fit: Use it when exact object pixels matter.

feedback.intrinsic: The task would require unnecessary pixel detail.

options.text: The text fields in the image
options.rationale: Extracting text fields is information extraction work. Classification identifies the image's main subject.
options.better_fit: Use it for receipt values or form fields.

feedback.intrinsic: The image could be labeled without extracting its fields.
feedback.instructional: Image classification labels the main subject.
